description: Collision, close-encounter, and merger scope decision: which contact models are product requirements, with detection radius, close-encounter policy, response, conservation, identity, rollback, and solver/MPI/SPH compatibility. Plummer softening is never a physical contact model.
gravity_only_preserved: Existing fixed-kdk-v1 and comoving-kdk-v2 trajectories, all solver families, PBC, MPI, restart (P9), SPH (P10 contract), and reduction diagnostics are unchanged; mergers add a deterministic detection-and-response stage, never a replacement.

detection.radius: physical contact radius R_contact, a per-run parameter in length units, distinct from the Plummer softening parameter
detection.trigger: a pair (i, j) merges when |r_ij| <= R_contact and the radial approach condition r_ij . v_ij < 0 holds at the detection stage on the deterministic local-neighbor graph
detection.softening_separation: zero-distance softening is never a collision or merger trigger; R_contact is an independent physical parameter documented in the run contracts

sticky-mergers-v1.name: perfectly inelastic sticky merger

equations.momentum: v_3 = (m_i v_i + m_j v_j) / m_3, so total momentum m v is exactly preserved
equations.position: x_3 equals the survivor position; the survivor is the particle with the lower stable ID
equations.energy_policy: kinetic deficit Delta_E = (1/2) mu |v_i - v_j|^2 with mu = m_i m_j / m_3 is recorded as the dissipated-energy diagnostic; the total-energy policy is documented: merger is not an energy-conserving stage, the deficit is explicit

sticky-mergers-v1.state_ownership: particles keep the existing SoA mass, position, and velocity boundaries; the removed particle leaves the active mask and its mass slot is zeroed; hydro density (P10) and solver caches are recomputed rather than merged
sticky-mergers-v1.determinism: simultaneous and transitive contact sets are resolved in ascending stable-ID order, one survivor per set; the merge set ordering is a deterministic sort over the local neighbor graph
sticky-mergers-v1.rollback: the pre-detection particle and acceleration state is checkpointed; any non-finite merged state or failure returns the recorded error and restores the checkpoint exactly
conservation_targets: total mass is exactly conserved across a merge
total momentum (canonical comoving momentum in the INT-005 frame) is exactly conserved
the dissipated kinetic budget equals the documented formula to round-off
identical contact sets and survivors on identical inputs (determinism)

identity_and_ownership.ids: the survivor keeps the lowest stable ID of the merged set; stable IDs (P9 restart) remain authoritative
identity_and_ownership.mpi: detection covers only the local deterministic neighbor graph; cross-ownership contact pairs transfer ownership to the rank of the survivor (lowest stable ID) before merging
identity_and_ownership.snapshots: published state contains only the active set; removed particles are absent, never ghosted

sticky-mergers-v1.boundaries: periodic boundaries via the existing PBC contract; the detection stage stays domain-agnostic like the integrator

rejected.elastic_restitution: reject: no clean-room bounce/restitution model exists and no product evidence justifies an energy-conserving contact deflection
rejected.contact_softening_as_collision: reject: confirmed non-goal of PHYS-001; Plummer softening never constitutes a physical contact or merger model
rejected.mass_loss_and_radiation_channels: reject: no clean-room sink, radiation, or mass-loss channel has product evidence
rejected.subgrid_fragmentation: reject: no unambiguous clean-room definition exists; fragmentation is not a Product requirement
rejected.gas_dynamic_mergers: reject at this scope: gas mergers belong to the P10 SPH family and are defined by the hydrodynamics contract, not by PHYS-001

interface_rules: detection reuses the deterministic local-neighbor index; no new solver entry point and no force-path change
the detection-and-response stage runs between integrator stages of the fixed split with full checkpoint rollback
no dynamic allocation after warmup; the merge-set sort is deterministic and in-place
compatible with Direct, Barnes-Hut, FMM, KIFMM, PM, and TreePM through the same neighbor contract, with MPI ownership transfer, and with the P10 SPH density summation
particle IDs, ownership, snapshots, and MPI migration remain coherent as specified in the identity_and_ownership block
